title: How many matchsticks make a row of triangles?
description: A row of five triangles is made from matchsticks, and neighbouring triangles share a side. The first triangle uses three sticks and each new one adds two, giving eleven. Keeko doubts this and says fifteen.
teaching_notes: One idea: a shared stick is counted once, so each new triangle adds two sticks and not three. Watch for students who multiply three by the number of triangles.

source: How many matchsticks make a row of 5 triangles that share sides?
video_script.why: The child learns to count the sticks of a growing row of triangles by seeing what each new triangle adds, which prepares the number sequences of the shape sequences in the book.
video_script.substitution: A row of five triangles made of matchsticks is used.
video_script.anchor: a row of five triangles made of matchsticks, with the shared sticks in a different colour
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko says five triangles need fifteen sticks, since each triangle needs three sticks. That counts every shared stick twice, so the real total is smaller and the bubble is struck.
video_script.payoff_line: A row of five triangles needs eleven matchsticks
maths_rules: each new triangle shares one side with the one before, so it adds 2 sticks
check: 5 triangles x 3 sticks = 15, minus 4 shared sticks = 11
video_script.design: A row of matchstick triangles grows one triangle at a time. The new sticks of each triangle are lit and counted, and the shared stick is marked.

<bookmark mark='ask'/>How many matchsticks make the whole row of triangles?

narration: <bookmark mark='second'/>Step two, add a second triangle next to the first.
<bookmark mark='new'/>One of its sides is already there, so it needs only two new sticks.
<bookmark mark='five'/>Three plus two gives five sticks for the first two triangles.

beats.on_screen: Step 3: each new triangle adds 2 sticks: 3, 5, 7, 9, then 9 + 2

narration: <bookmark mark='rule'/>Step three, every new triangle adds two sticks again. The counts are three, five, seven and nine.
<bookmark mark='last'/>The fifth triangle adds two more sticks to the nine we already have.

marks.ans: the whole row and the count are boxed

narration: <bookmark mark='ans'/>A row of five triangles needs eleven matchsticks. Nine plus two is eleven.

beats.on_screen: Keeko with a raised hand beside the board
narration: <bookmark mark='hand'/>Keeko has raised a hand. Let us check the doubt and solve it.

beats.on_screen: Keeko's bubble says 15 sticks; the shared sticks are marked and counted twice; the bubble is struck through in the warning colour

marks.shared: the four shared sticks are marked, each with a two

narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko thinks five triangles need fifteen sticks, since each triangle needs three sticks.
<bookmark mark='shared'/>But the triangles share sides, and a shared stick is counted only once.
<bookmark mark='strike'/>Fifteen counts every shared stick twice, so the real total must be smaller.
